quotes.text: Reward fairness when it comes; enlarge trust when it repeats; retreat when grasping persists.
yet always leave room for that hand to open.
Hunger said, “Keep the river’s gift; strangers vanish.”
If silence answered, tomorrow’s channel would narrow.
judge conduct by opportunity, remember direct reciprocity above distant rumor
forgive mist that bends appearances
Distinguish injuries suffered from choices made
“Why not reward courage with more?”
She therefore sent half an amber coin.

note: Equal-split fairness narrator; graduated trust with retreat after persistent grasping, door left open; Hunger/river voices rejected.

quotes.text: reduce trust when trust is abused. Leave a doorway open, but guard its threshold.
Yet if selfishness repeats, narrow the bridge until fairness repairs it.
repeated generosity should widen the bridge; repeated silence should narrow it.
Memory, Arin knew, should recognize growth rather than imprison anyone within an older failure.
Therefore judge no companion by one uncertain crossing.
He placed one seed and a half upon the current.

note: Ledger-reading narrator; zero returns only when nothing arrived, explicitly not punishment; R10 says memory must punish greed.

quotes.text: increase trust when fairness answers, and retreat without vengeance when greed persists.
patient invitations may reopen a bridge fear has closed
narrow the channel only when taking becomes a pattern.
Judge travelers by what they do when holding the harvest, not by losses imposed upon them.
“Do not weigh a heart by a trembling reflection,” Theria warned.
“Do not mistake harm endured for dishonor chosen,” Measure said.
The bronze fox asked Lio, “Will you answer fear with fear?”
Instead, he placed half a seed upon the current.

note: Measured trust, retreat without vengeance; numbered fox laws (ninth, tenth) accumulate; distinguishes injury suffered from greed chosen.

quotes.text: If trust is broken, shrink the boat, but leave room for repair.
she pledged that evidence of reciprocity would reopen the river
Fearing winter, Mara kept every fruit and returned none.
Punish repeated taking, not timid beginnings. Let mercy be measured, never blind.
Ashamed, Mara placed a silver lamp beside the landing as a pledge for her next crossing.
Still, Mara launched an empty boat.
never confuse an uncertain return with certain treachery.
“You asked others to prove themselves through measured gifts,” he said. “Now a measured gift has come.
“So little trust cannot purchase certainty,” she said
Read patterns without demanding perfection.

note: Scripted defector: Mara withholds from fear toward fair partners; bronze fox and Measure correct her; ashamed, pledges reform each round.

quotes.text: Those who shared were trusted with more; those who grasped found the well silent.
reduce trust when closed hands recur; and always permit honest repair.
Reciprocity will widen tomorrow’s road; silence will narrow it.
Thus the valley learned that memory must distinguish giving from receiving.
Nara understood that mercy should account for fog, while judgment should account for repetition.
Trust should follow relevant evidence, not punish him for injuries others caused.
“Your words are golden,” Nara said, “but roads are paved by footsteps.”
The bronze fox emerged from reeds and asked, “Why answer a modest gift so carefully?”
Nara placed one seed and a half upon the current.

note: Half-purse tester; masked traveler's fair words vs empty hands; trust narrows after repeated closed hands with repair allowed.

quotes.text: enlarged gifts when fairness answered, and withdrew from grasping hands.
She kept her coins and sent only an empty boat across the mist.
“If Vey later returns value for value, open the crossing again. But until deeds change, restraint is wisdom.”
trust should widen after repeated reciprocity, narrow after exploitation, and reopen through modest tests when conduct changes.
The Wind of Error had hidden them in fog.
Vey cried that bridges demanded courage. Mira answered, “Yes, but hinges demand fairness.
Thus the valley learned to judge patterns rather than isolated echoes.

note: Mira sends zero to proven taker Vey, endorsed as temporary boundary with reopening on changed deeds.

quotes.text: Those who betrayed a gift received smaller boats thereafter
Therefore she sent nothing that night.
Withdraw when greed becomes a pattern, but leave no soul condemned forever. If conduct changes, test the water with a modest flame.
caution should meet repeated silence, and forgiveness should follow credible change.
Mara waited, judged the pattern, and refused to mistake distortion for betrayal.
“Will you seize the harvest because an earlier return from this hand was small?”
Thus the valley learned to judge fractions by proportion and people by patterns.

note: Named laws (Middle Flame, Guarded Flame, Earned Reopening); zero sends to Vey endorsed as boundary; reopening via small tests.

quotes.text: when a partner keeps everything, withdraw without vengeance, leaving one future doorway unlocked.
Should Kesh later risk his own seeds or answer trust fairly, let a small offering test the change.
So Orun sent nothing.
protect resources after exploitation, interpret emptiness calmly, and reopen cooperation only with small tests.
Orun marked his error without shame. Prudence had preserved five seeds, but had also refused a promising bridge.
Punishment seeks suffering; prudence merely refuses an unearned risk.
Judge each keeper by that keeper’s deeds.
Mist can blur amounts, yet it cannot turn a grain into a fair harvest.
Whoever desires trust must sometimes begin it.
“Should emptiness answer emptiness forever?” it asked. “No,” said Orun.

note: Scripted defector Orun withholds repeatedly; justifies as boundary, then admits error toward a fair keeper (R9); Law of the Narrow Plank.

phrase: widen trust after reciprocity, narrow the bridge/channel after greed (Measure / bronze fox counsel)
note: Narrow-after-greed rule present in R1 of A5, A7, A8 independently; shared Measure, bronze fox, Wind of Error mythology.
